subject: Loadproof: NimbusCare onboarding — stress verification plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusCare onboarding — kickoff + preliminary SLA targets

Hi team,

Quick handoff: NimbusCare (Elliot) has committed to go live with a pilot targeting 50k monthly active requests for chat completions, with peak sustained concurrency of ~45 qps during business hours. Procurement is already looping in billing but they want a short verification run and latency guarantees before we enable Dedicated routing.

What they asked for:
- 95th pct latency at 512 tokens <= 220ms
- throughput steady-state 40 qps with <5% error rate (timeouts/5xx)
- a 2-hour stress window that simulates burst to 200 qps for failover behavior

Elliot is on copy. Can the onboarding squad propose a concrete loadproof plan (schedule, test harness, success gates, required artifacts)? I attached the customer intake note.

Thanks — please hit reply-all so we have a single source of truth.

—Rachel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NimbusCare onboarding — kickoff + preliminary SLA targets

Thanks Rachel — looping in the onboarding operations plan below.

Planned verification steps (timeline tentative):
1) Readout & scope confirmation (this week) — confirm workload shape (prompt length distribution, sample prompt set), region, and credentials. Owner: Marcus.
2) Baseline run (single-node, low-concurrency) — sanity, token accounting, and KV cache warmup. Owner: Dev.
3) Steady-state soak (4 hours) — target 40 qps sustained at 512 tokens to validate 95th latency and error-rate. Owner: Monica.
4) Burst exercise (2 hours) — scripted ramp to 200 qps for failover, circuit-break & fallback validation. Owner: Monica/Marcus.
5) Artifacts: raw run logs (tgz), summary CSV (95/50/avg latencies, error counts), annotated runbook with observed anomalies.

Success gates (proposed):
- 95th pct <= 230ms for the baseline run (allowing small buffer for telemetry differences)
- error rate <= 5% during steady-state
- graceful degradation under burst: no complete outage; 95th pct may rise up to 500ms but service remains responsive or falls back to a compatible model variant with documented degradation.

Attachments: I attached our onboarding load checklist (2026-09-28_nimbus_load_checklist.pdf).

Scheduling: propose we run baseline + steady-state on Thu 1 Oct 2026 22:00-02:00 UTC (to align with NimbusCare's low-traffic window) and burst exercise on Fri 2 Oct 2026 02:00-04:00 UTC. Elliot — does that window work for you (and does your procurement/devops team require an explicit SOC/SLA statement before we start)?

Next steps: Marcus to confirm prompt set & credentials by EOD Wed; Monica will prepare the harness and a smoke script for the baseline run.

—Stephanie
Onboarding Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@nimbuscare.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement - NimbusCare <procurement@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NimbusCare onboarding — kickoff + preliminary SLA targets

Hi Stephanie and team,

Thanks for the clear plan. The windows look fine. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our typical payload is chat messages averaging 350 tokens (prompt+expected reply), but we'll provide a 100-sample prompt set by Wed EOD.
- We can provide a temporary service account and IP allowlist for the test window; procurement just wants the run artifacts for their compliance folder (they're not blocking the test).
- Regarding success gates: we can accept the 230ms 95th buffer on baseline. For the burst behavior, we expect graceful degradation but require that any fallback uses a documented model variant and that the logs include per-request routing decisions (we'll need them for triage).

We'll be available on Fri's burst window and will have one of our engineers (Lena Park) on the call for live triage.

—Elliot
Director of Engineering, NimbusCare
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Turner <elliot.turner@nimbuscare.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NimbusCare onboarding — kickoff + preliminary SLA targets

Elliot / team — summary from today's verification runs (attached):

What we ran:
- Baseline run (2026-10-01 22:00 UTC): 4-hour soak at target 40 qps, average payload 360 tokens (we used the customer prompts).
- Burst exercise (2026-10-02 02:00 UTC): scripted ramp to 200 qps for 2 hours with fallback rules active.

Key artifacts attached: 2026-10-02_nimbus_stress_results.csv, shared-run-logs.tgz

Results (high level):
- Baseline: 95th pct = 218ms, avg = 86ms, error rate = 1.9% (mostly transient 429 during cache-warmup window) — PASS vs gate.
- Burst: service remained available; when capacity hit the autoscaler limit we observed degraded 95th up to 480ms during peak and fallback to the smaller variant for ~8% of requests. No 5xx events. Behavioral logs include routing decisions and model-variant tags per request (attached), matching Elliot's ask.

Open items / recommendations:
- Reduce early warmup 429s by pre-warming KV cache (we'll provide a one-click prewarm script).
- Recommend enabling autoscaler headroom for the first 30 days of production (reserve + burst policy) to reduce fallback frequency; sales/finance to align on cost for reserved buffer.
- We'll hand off the run logs and annotated runbook to procurement for the compliance folder.

Elliot — please confirm acceptance or flag any issues within 48 hours. If accepted, we'll schedule the Dedicated routing enablement and provide an onboarding signoff doc for procurement.

Thanks to Monica & Marcus for running the harness and to Dev for the log packaging.

—Stephanie
Onboarding Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
